relations.supporting_evidence: Both population annotations refer to PEC-Direct Cohort 2; S19 explicitly cites S18 as an earlier group.
relations.contradictory_or_limiting_evidence: Earlier versus optimized cadre and different enrollment/device strategy counter an automatic same-cohort inference, but do not prove mutually exclusive people. No affirmative source contradiction establishing disjointness is available.
relations.decision_rationale: Neither same, directional subset nor distinct_within_program is established; retain S19 participant overlap uncertain, not presumed distinct.
relations.human_decision: Decide whether approved aggregate cadre wording explicitly excludes repeat participation across these two full targets. If not, adopt uncertain with no direction; do not infer distinctness from chronology.
relations.change_threshold: distinct_within_program requires explicit aggregate non-overlap/re-enrollment exclusion covering both complete targets. A subset requires complete inclusion and direction; same requires full membership equivalence, not common trial registration.

relations.supporting_evidence: Known partial overlap and inherited S23 cross-reference annotations support shared membership context, not a counted match or complete inclusion.
relations.contradictory_or_limiting_evidence: Known overlap rules out distinct_within_program. Full targets of 17 and 15 counter same-target equivalence; the smaller site target does not by itself prove it is wholly within the publication data-cut target.
relations.decision_rationale: No partial-overlap enum exists. Preserve known partial overlap in the note while recommending uncertain with no accepted subset direction or exact matched count.
relations.human_decision: Accept uncertain while preserving known partial overlap, unless @aditmer can verify aggregate evidence that every S23 target member belongs to the exact S18 target. Cross-reference clues alone are insufficient.
relations.change_threshold: Only if complete S23-in-S18 inclusion is verified on both frozen sides propose subset/to_is_subset_of_from in this S18-to-S23 row. Never invent a matched count; do not amend vocabulary to force an overlap value.

relations.supporting_evidence: S18's aggregate population is described as a Cohort 2 publication selection; S20 is the related Cohort 2 registry report.
relations.contradictory_or_limiting_evidence: Publication data-cut selection is not the registry STARTED accounting definition. Shared NCT03163511 and Cohort 2 labels do not establish inclusion in the exact history-v20 target or endpoint compatibility.
relations.decision_rationale: An S18-to-S20 subset is plausible but not verified under the frozen registry version; uncertainty is a membership decision, not a missing-outcome inference.
relations.human_decision: Decide whether every member of S18's full publication selection is included in v20's Cohort 2 target under compatible enrollment/implantation accounting; otherwise adopt uncertain.
relations.change_threshold: subset/from_is_subset_of_to requires an explicit aggregate inclusion statement plus verified v20 cohort definition/data-cut mapping. Registry totals, planned labels or a publication citation alone cannot satisfy it.

relations.supporting_evidence: S19 cites S23 as an earlier study group within the shared program; S23 is the full Vancouver site population.
relations.contradictory_or_limiting_evidence: A later optimized cadre is not automatically the earlier site group, but chronology/device differences do not exclude repeat participation. S18/S23 overlap is not transitive proof of S19 membership.
relations.decision_rationale: S19 overlap remains uncertain; neither a site association nor earlier-report citation proves overlap, disjointness or subset direction.
relations.human_decision: Decide whether aggregate source prose excludes all S23-target participation in the optimized S19 cadre. If it does not, adopt uncertain rather than infer distinctness from enrollment timing.
relations.change_threshold: distinct_within_program requires two-sided aggregate exclusion of repeat membership across the complete targets; same/subset requires explicit equivalence/inclusion. @aditmer must verify the S23 side under Path B.

relations.supporting_evidence: Inherited S19 prose places the ten-recipient optimized cadre in Cohort 2; S20 is the related registry report.
relations.contradictory_or_limiting_evidence: Changed device/cadre strategy and enrollment interval need mapping to v20 cohort categories. Neither common registration nor a registry flow count proves the optimized ten are included in that frozen registry target.
relations.decision_rationale: Candidate cadre-to-registry inclusion is not established by the available two-sided evidence; preserve S19 overlap uncertain.
relations.human_decision: Decide whether the v20 Cohort 2 definition includes all ten optimized recipients despite relevant cadre/device amendments; without aggregate membership verification adopt uncertain.
relations.change_threshold: subset/from_is_subset_of_to requires verified v20 categories and explicit inclusion of the entire optimized cadre. Do not use response subsets, endpoint denominators or current-API data as membership proof.

relations.supporting_evidence: The Vancouver site target shares NCT03163511 with the related Cohort 2 registry report.
relations.contradictory_or_limiting_evidence: S23 allocated/implanted/overall-analysis membership is not automatically v20 STARTED membership. The single-site target cannot stand for all registry participants; S18 overlap does not independently prove site-to-registry inclusion.
relations.decision_rationale: Plausible site-to-Cohort-2 subset remains unverified against both frozen targets, with no authorized new Path B inspection.
relations.human_decision: Have @aditmer decide whether all 15 site-target participants map to history-v20 Cohort 2 with compatible allocation/implantation/STARTED definitions; otherwise adopt uncertain.
relations.change_threshold: subset/from_is_subset_of_to requires verified aggregate site inclusion and exact v20 accounting on both sides. A shared registry ID, site label or numerical comparison alone is insufficient.
